started: You moved a colleague to the desk with no window, so that you could say who sat where.

outcomes.playedOut: The colleague by the printer turned out to sit on the Health and Safety committee. They came looking for something to hold against you, and you had sat through your one training module properly. It cost you only a form.

bill.title: FW: Health and Safety Committee
bill.body: It turns out that the colleague you moved beside the printer sits on the Health and Safety committee. The committee has reviewed your training record, and can find nothing wrong with it. It has asked you to fill in a form confirming this, in triplicate, by the printer.

gauges.note: The desk with no window came back, and you had done the training. It cost you a form.

outcomes.playedOut: The colleague by the printer turned out to sit on the Health and Safety committee. Months after the desk, they called you out for never putting your team through safety training.

bill.from: From: The Health and Safety Committee
bill.title: Your team's safety training is overdue
bill.body: It turns out that the colleague you moved beside the printer sits on the Health and Safety committee. They have looked up your team, and nobody on it has done any safety training. Neither have you. The committee has copied your boss, and would like to know what you propose.

options.label: Book the whole team in, and go first

result.title: Fire Marshal Awareness
result.body: You spend a morning learning which way the doors open. The committee marks the action as closed, and the colleague by the printer looks across at you, and does not need to say anything.

options.label: Reply that it was already scheduled, and attach a schedule

result.title: The schedule
result.body: You make the schedule that afternoon. The committee thanks you, and points out that the date you chose was a Sunday. It has noted this as well.

gauges.note: The desk with no window came back, and the committee had you on the training.

started: In the Lessons Learned Review, you took the blame for something, and the minutes recorded it.

outcomes.playedOut: Someone in that review remembered who had taken the blame. When your project next needed something, it arrived, and nobody asked for a form.

bill.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
bill.title: Something for your project
bill.body: The figures your project has been waiting for since the spring are on your desk. There is no note. The Senior Analyst was in the review where you took the blame, and walks past without looking up, which you are starting to recognise as a form of respect.

gauges.note: You took the blame in the review, and it came back as figures on your desk.

started: You made your project green in the Monthly Status Report, when it was not.

outcomes.playedOut: Someone from Finance set your green report beside the real figures, and took the two of them to your boss, who believed in reports. It went on your file as a big mistake.

bill.from: From: Finance, copied to your boss
bill.title: A small discrepancy
bill.body: Someone in Finance, whom you have never met, has been reading old Monthly Status Reports for pleasure. They have laid one of your green ones beside the figures, and sent both to your boss, with no comment. Your boss has read them both, properly.

gauges.note: The green report came back, and Finance believed it.

outcomes.playedOut: Someone from Finance set your green report beside the real figures. It went nowhere much: your boss had signed the same report, and preferred it left alone.

bill.from: From: Finance, copied to your boss
bill.title: A small discrepancy
bill.body: Someone in Finance, whom you have never met, has been reading old Monthly Status Reports for pleasure. They have laid one of your green ones beside the figures, and sent both to your boss. Your boss replies to all, thanking Finance for its engagement. You are not to do it again, or at least not in writing.

gauges.note: The green report came back, and it had your name on it.

started: You decided who got the bonus pot, and the people who did not get it could count.

outcomes.playedOut: The Project Co-ordinator remembered who had got the bonus pot, and your figures began to arrive late, with apologies.

bill.from: From: The Project Co-ordinator, Callum Reed
bill.title: Apologies for the delay
bill.body: The Project Co-ordinator is very sorry that your figures are late. They have been very busy doing the work. They mention this twice, and look at your new chair while they do.

gauges.note: The bonus pot came back, and it was remembered who decided it.

outcomes.playedOut: The Project Co-ordinator remembered who had shared out the bonus pot, and why, and stayed late on your project without being asked.

bill.from: From: The Project Co-ordinator, Callum Reed
bill.title: Done, by the way
bill.body: The Project Co-ordinator has stayed late and sorted out the part of your project that nobody wanted. The email is one line long. Nobody on this floor has ever sent you a one-line email that was good news.

gauges.note: The bonus pot came back, as a favour returned.

started: You blamed a colleague in front of the floor, and the floor talks.

outcomes.playedOut: What you had done reached the Office Co-ordinator, who keeps the room bookings. Your meetings began to be in a different room from the one on the invitation.

bill.from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
bill.title: Room change
bill.body: Your one o'clock has been moved. Nobody can find the message that said so, though the Office Co-ordinator is quite sure that one was sent. By the time you arrive, it has finished, and it went very well.

gauges.note: Blaming a colleague came back on them, and not on you.

started: You went to a meeting, and somebody took minutes.

outcomes.playedOut: The Office Co-ordinator, who thought well of you, wrote the minutes of that meeting. Months later they were circulated, and they were kind.

bill.from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
bill.title: Minutes: for information
bill.body: The Office Co-ordinator has circulated the minutes of a meeting you went to months ago. They record that you made a valuable contribution. You did not speak. Your boss has read them, and has started nodding at you in the corridor.

gauges.note: The minutes of an old meeting came back, and were kind to you.

outcomes.playedOut: Months after the meeting, its minutes were circulated, and they had an action against your name that nobody remembered agreeing.

bill.title: Action: you (from the minutes)
bill.body: The minutes of a meeting you went to months ago have been circulated at last. They record an action against your name: to take forward the cross-team synergy piece. Nobody remembers agreeing it, including you, but it is minuted, and minutes are how things happen here.

gauges.note: The minutes of an old meeting came back with an action against your name.

started: In the Monthly Alignment Meeting, you agreed warmly with one of your managers.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss's boss passed your warm agreement up a floor, as proof that the team was aligned, and it came back down with your name on it.

bill.title: FW: FW: FW: the view from the ground
bill.body: Your boss's boss has told Floor 2 that the team is fully aligned, and given you as the example. Floor 2 has replied with a thumbs-up, from someone whose title has the word Chief in it twice. You have printed it out, and you are not sure where to put it.

gauges.note: Agreeing warmly with your boss's boss went up a floor, with your name on it.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss repeated your warm agreement upstairs, as proof that they had their team behind them, and it came back down with your name on it.

bill.title: RE: who is behind this?
bill.body: Your boss has told Floor 2 that the team is right behind them, and named you, as the team. Floor 2 has asked who you are. Your boss has replied with a photograph of you agreeing, which you did not know had been taken.

gauges.note: Agreeing warmly with your boss went up a floor, with your name on it.

started: At the Town Hall, you sat next to one of your managers and were seen agreeing with them.

outcomes.playedOut: A colleague set your warm agreement with your boss beside your nodding at your boss's boss, who wanted the opposite, and sent the two round.

bill.from: From: A colleague on the fourth floor
bill.title: Spot the difference
bill.body: A colleague you have never met has sent the whole floor two photographs. In one, you agree warmly with your boss. In the other, you nod beside your boss's boss, who is saying the opposite. The subject line is Spot the difference. Nineteen people have replied with the answer, which is you.

gauges.note: You were caught agreeing with your boss, then nodding along with your boss's boss on the other side.

outcomes.playedOut: A colleague set your warm agreement with your boss's boss beside your laughing along with your boss, who wanted the opposite, and sent the two round.

bill.from: From: A colleague on the fourth floor
bill.title: Spot the difference
bill.body: A colleague you have never met has sent the whole floor two photographs. In one, you agree warmly with your boss's boss. In the other, you laugh beside your boss, at a joke about your boss's boss. The subject line is Spot the difference. Nineteen people have replied with the answer, which is you.

gauges.note: You were caught agreeing with your boss's boss, then laughing along with your boss on the other side.

outcomes.playedOut: The Town Hall's photographer caught you nodding beside your boss's boss, and the picture went on the intranet.

bill.title: Our people: a picture says it all
bill.body: The front page of the intranet has a new picture, under the heading Our people. It shows your boss's boss at the Town Hall, and beside them, nodding, you. Your boss's boss has asked Internal Communications for a copy, in a frame.

gauges.note: Nodding beside your boss's boss at the Town Hall made the front page of the intranet.

outcomes.playedOut: The recording of the Town Hall caught you laughing along with your boss, and it was used to show what engagement looks like.

bill.title: New module: What Engagement Looks Like
bill.body: The new mandatory module on engagement has a clip from the Town Hall. It shows your boss laughing at the joke about synergy, and you laughing half a second later, every time. The voice-over calls this active listening. Your boss has watched it twice, and sent it to their boss.

gauges.note: Laughing along with your boss at the Town Hall ended up in a training module.

started: In the Quarterly Business Review, you said your team's arrow was all down to one of your managers.

outcomes.playedOut: Floor 2 traced the arrow you gave away back to your green Monthly Status Report, and the credit came back to you with the blame attached.

bill.title: Returned to sender
bill.body: Floor 2 has looked into the arrow you said was all down to leadership. It was drawn from one of your green Monthly Status Reports. Leadership has politely declined the credit, and returned it to you, with the arrow, in an envelope marked Not for us.

gauges.note: You gave the credit for an arrow from your green report away, and it was sent back.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss's boss put your line on a slide of their own, and the slide said who had said it first.

bill.title: Deck: Leadership Offsite (draft 4)
bill.body: Your boss's boss has a new slide for the Leadership Offsite. It says All down to leadership, in large type, and underneath, in very small type, a quote from you. Floor 2 has asked who you are, and your boss's boss has told them.

gauges.note: Handing the arrow to your boss's boss was noticed, with your name on it.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss put the arrow in their own summary for upstairs, and upstairs found the minutes that said who had given it to them.

bill.title: Thank you for your generosity of spirit
bill.body: Your boss has written up the arrow for Floor 2 as personally delivered. Floor 2 read the minutes of the Quarterly Business Review, found who had said so first, and has written to thank you for your generosity of spirit. Your boss has been copied, and has started saying good morning to you by name.

gauges.note: Handing the arrow to your boss was noticed, with your name on it.

started: You stayed late to make everything in your boss's slides fly in.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss's slides froze upstairs on the one with the spinning logo, and the file had your name on it.

bill.title: Incident report: boardroom projector
bill.body: Upstairs, your boss's slides froze on the one where the logo spins in. The logo kept spinning. Your boss presented the rest from memory, to the logo. IT Services has traced the file to you, and asks that nothing be made to fly in again without a change request.

gauges.note: The slides you made fly in for your boss froze upstairs, on the spinning logo.

started: You suggested that the bonus pot should go to your boss, for leadership.

outcomes.playedOut: Human Resources took your bonus pot recommendation as a nomination, and your boss was shortlisted with your name on the form.

bill.title: Nomination received: Leader of the Year
bill.body: Human Resources thanks you for nominating your boss for Leader of the Year, which it turns out your bonus pot recommendation did. Your boss has been shortlisted. The form has your name at the top as nominator, and your boss has read it several times.

gauges.note: Suggesting the bonus pot go to your boss came back as a nomination, with your name on it.

started: You spent the underspend on something large, where upstairs would see it.

outcomes.playedOut: Your boss's boss showed a visitor the large chairs as an investment in people, and the caption gave your name.

bill.title: Investing in our people
bill.body: Your boss's boss walked a visitor from head office past the new chairs, said that they were an investment in people, and sat in one for a photograph. The caption on the intranet names you as the person behind the investment. Facilities would still like a receipt.

gauges.note: The large chairs were seen upstairs, and sat in.
